claimed_invariant: External and ordinary sequence messages share one autoactivation rule. With autoactivate enabled, a solid normal/open-headed incoming external message activates its participant, while a dotted normal/open-headed outgoing external message deactivates its participant; the accepted change immediately updates subsequent return ownership.
causal_divergence: Rust calls autoactivation_for only from try_message. Both try_external_message branches leave activation unset unless the source has an explicit ++, --, or !! suffix. Consequently an outgoing dotted boundary message leaves a completed callee on the return stack, and an incoming solid boundary message fails to create the activation segment that a later return should close. The first wrong external event then rotates every subsequent return pair and lifeline envelope. Rust's spacing and paint projections also leave their last-message fallback pointing at the pre-return message after synthesizing a bare return; Java addMessage records each synthesized return as the newest EventWithDeactivate, so a consecutive return reverses the preceding return rather than an older external message.
planned_model_change: Apply the existing autoactivation_for rule after inline arrow style parsing in both external-message branches whenever no explicit activation suffix is present.
